page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration is built on the x86_64 architecture and includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation. The CPU architecture incorporates an extensive cache hierarchy, consisting of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16, alongside Intel AMX matrix multiplication acceleration features.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local storage disks, requiring attached network persistent storage for disk operations. No graphics processing units are provisioned with this instance type, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. In memory benchmarks, the platform demonstrates sustained throughput of 117.6 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 67.32 GB/sec for large-block writes, reaching 1107.55 GB/sec within cached memory ranges.

Benchmark results place the instance broadly within average performance bands across standard compute and memory evaluations. The system scored 1855.0 points in Geekbench single-core and 11352.0 points in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21504.31. In specialized AI execution, LLM text generation using a small 135M model achieved 282.68 tokens per second, registering in the upper quartile of comparable systems, while medium 7B model prompt evaluation processed at 92.51 tokens per second.

With balanced compute and memory capacity, Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is suitable for enterprise application runtimes, Redis caching tiers handling high operation volumes, static web serving clusters, continuous integration compilation tasks, and lightweight quantized language model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 16 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of memory across 8 physical Intel x86_64 cores. Featuring a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration includes dedicated CPU allocation with hyper-threading, a 260 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating remote persistent storage for file systems. Benchmark performance reflects middle-tier consistency across multi-threaded computational workloads, achieving 11352.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 17.13 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware acceleration instructions support above-average throughput on lightweight CPU-based language model generation. The instance profile is well structured for web serving, database management, software compilation, and scalable enterprise application backends.
